The Colour Rendering Index (CRI) measures how accurately a light source reproduces colors compared to natural light.  
Incandescent lamps produce light by heating a filament, emitting a continuous spectrum similar to sunlight, giving them a CRI close to 100 — the highest among common lamp types.  
LEDs and fluorescents often have lower CRI values (though high-CRI versions exist), and high-pressure sodium vapour lamps have very poor CRI.
